title: Cohomology over an object is cohomology on its localized site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a Grothendieck site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $W$ an object of $\mathcal C$, and $G$ an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal C$. Give the slice category $\mathcal C/W$ the topology in which a family covers precisely when its underlying family covers in $\mathcal C$; it has final object $\mathrm{id}_W:W\to W$. Write $G|_W$ for the sheaf on $\mathcal C/W$ given by $(V\to W)\mapsto G(V)$. Restriction $G\mapsto G|_W$ sends injective abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C$ to injective abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C/W$. For every $q\geq0$, the cohomology $H^q(W,G)=R^q\Gamma(W,-)(G)$ over $W$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] is canonically isomorphic to $H^q(\mathrm{id}_W,G|_W)=R^q\Gamma(\mathrm{id}_W,-)(G|_W)$ computed on the localized site $\mathcal C/W$, naturally in $G$ and in maps of objects $W'\to W$.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03F3 (lemma-cohomology-of-open), parts (1)-(2); abelian sheaves are modules over the constant integer sheaf

proof.text: The slice category has the stated Grothendieck topology by definition, and $\mathrm{id}_W:W\to W$ is final because every object $V\to W$ has its unique structure morphism to $\mathrm{id}_W$. The assignment $(V\to W)\mapsto G(V)$ with the inherited restriction maps is the restriction sheaf on the slice.

source.place: Sites, Section 00XZ (section-localize), definition of the localized site

proof.text: The extension-by-zero statement gives a left adjoint $j_{W!}$ to restriction, and says that both $j_{W!}$ and restriction are exact.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Section 03DH and Lemmas 03DI-03DJ

proof.text: Since restriction is the right adjoint of the exact functor $j_{W!}$, the right-adjoint-preserves-injectives lemma implies that restriction sends injective abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C$ to injective abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C/W$. Together with exactness of restriction from step 2, an injective resolution $G\to I^\bullet$ restricts to an injective resolution $G|_W\to I^\bullet|_W$.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemmas 03DI-03DJ; Homology, Lemma 015Z

proof.text: By the definition of restriction, evaluation at the final object is degreewise $\Gamma(\mathrm{id}_W,I^\bullet|_W)=I^\bullet(W)$. The cohomology definition computes $H^q(W,G)$ from $I^\bullet(W)$ and computes $H^q(\mathrm{id}_W,G|_W)$ from $\Gamma(\mathrm{id}_W,I^\bullet|_W)$, so the identity of complexes induces the claimed canonical isomorphism.

For a morphism $G\to G'$ the induced maps of injective resolutions can be chosen as chain maps; any two choices are chain-homotopic by the injective-resolution lifting lemma, and restriction carries the homotopy to the slice, so the cohomology isomorphism is natural in $G$. For a morphism $W'\to W$, the relocalization identification $\mathcal C/W'=(\mathcal C/W)/(W'/W)$ and the sectionwise definition of restriction identify the two comparison complexes; hence the same construction is natural in $W'\to W$.
